title: Watermark-driven KV demotion with hotset sampling and GPU slab coalescing
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Goal: implement a watermark-driven demotion policy for the paged/blocked KV cache that reduces GPU OOMs and swap churn while preserving hot-token latency during continuous batching. This ticket covers: design of a lightweight hotset sampler, columnar/tiling layout inside slab pages to minimize fragmentation, an async demotion pipeline with priority lanes, and a GPU-coalescing pre-swap pass that merges adjacent small victim blocks before issuing PCIe/NVLink transfers. The feature must integrate with existing paged KV allocator and the residency budget controller, and expose runtime flags for canary testing and gradual rollout.
background: We currently observe two failure modes during high-concurrency continuous batching: (1) noisy eviction churn where many small KV slots are repeatedly exchanged between host and GPU, causing PCIe saturation and tail latency spikes; (2) hotset displacement where tokens with strong temporal locality get demoted prematurely because eviction is purely LRU by slot, not by token affinity. Previous work (see ENG-62183, ENG-56210) introduced slab allocators and residency budgets but left room for smarter demotion heuristics and pre-swap coalescing. This ticket aims to close that gap with minimal serving overhead.
design_summary: 1) Watermark demotion: introduce two watermarks on per-GPU residency budgets: soft_watermark and hard_watermark. When residency > soft_watermark, background demotion picks low-affinity candidates; when > hard_watermark, trigger preemptive demotion of lowest-affinity slots synchronously for new allocations. 2) Hotset sampler: probabilistic sampler that tracks access counts decayed over time per token-key (hashed) to approximate hotness without full per-slot counters. The sampler feeds affinity scores used during demotion decisions. 3) Columnar tiling: reorganize slab page layout into columnar tiles (tile_size ~ 64KB) that pack KV entries with similar lifetime/affinity to enable coalesced DMA and lower internal fragmentation. 4) Coalescing pre-swap: before issuing host<->GPU transfers, scan victim tiles and merge contiguous free/evicted subregions into larger chunks to reduce number of PCIe transfers. 5) Async eviction lanes: two lanes (background_low_priority, foreground_high_priority). Background eviction runs opportunistically and uses sampler scores; foreground eviction handles allocation stalls and honor hard_watermark with preemption of least-affine tiles. 6) Telemetry: new metrics - affinity_hit_ratio, coalesced_transfer_bytes, avg_victim_chunk_count, eviction_retries, softness_ratio (time spent > soft_watermark), and p99_allocate_latency.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Sampling adds CPU overhead; mitigate with probabilistic sampling and CPU offload to low-priority worker threads. - Columnar tiling requires online compaction when tile fragmentation grows; we favor a background compactor with throttling. - Coalescing reduces transfer count but adds latency to eviction path; ensure foreground lane bypasses coalescing when allocation latency is critical. - Complexity increases risk of regressions; plan gated rollout with telemetry checks and automatic rollback thresholds.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Instrumentation and sampler prototype (native hotset sampler as a library in runtime). Add metrics and unit tests.
Phase 2: Implement watermark thresholds and integrate sampler into eviction policy. Add config flags to tune soft/hard watermarks per-GPU.
Phase 3: Implement columnar tiling layout in slab allocator and mapping for tiled pages. Provide migration path for existing pages (on-touch rewrite).
Phase 4: Implement coalescing pre-swap pass and async eviction lanes. Add heuristics for when to coalesce vs immediate transfer.
Phase 5: Performance benchmarks, soak tests, canary rollout, and runbook updates.
acceptance_criteria: P99 generation latency for seeded throughput scenarios does not degrade by >5% compared to baseline when residency below soft_watermark.
Under sustained oversubscription load (1.5x expected working set), coalesced_transfer_bytes reduces transfer count by >=40% and PCIe bandwidth tail reduces by >=30% in lab runs.
Hotset sampler keeps affinity_hit_ratio >= 0.85 for synthetic skewed workloads (zipfian 0.9) across 12h soak test.
No increase in OOM incidents on dedicated small-GPU configurations during canary (monitor eviction_retries and p99_allocate_latency).
Feature gate exists and can be toggled per-cluster; automatic rollback triggers if p99_allocate_latency rises >20% or eviction_retries doubles in canary window.

comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Gupta: Initial spike shows hotset sampler with 10% CPU overhead under 2000 QPS; using probabilistic sampling reduced overhead to ~2.5%. Need microbench to pin cost at 95th percentile.

2026-03-04 - Lena Park (review): Love the watermark idea. Two asks: (1) add a failsafe that bypasses coalescing for allocations where latency budget < 3ms, (2) document how sampler hashes keys to avoid skew collision.

2026-03-06 - Miguel Torres: Implemented sampler prototype and unit tests. Pushed experimental metrics to bench_dashboard. Observed affinity_hit_ratio 0.82 initially; tuning decay window to 30s improved to 0.88.

2026-03-08 - Security review (note by Priya Raman): No secrets introduced. Confirmed host transfer coalescing respects DMA region alignment and no user data is leaked across tenant-mapped pages. No further action required.

2026-03-10 - SRE (Jamal Reed): Ran 4h soak with synthetic Zipf workload on a 4xA100 test rig. Coalesced transfers reduced number of PCIe operations by 47% and p99 allocation latency improved by 18% during oversubscription. Observed a rare race in foreground eviction path under sudden spike; added a mid-priority lock to mitigate.
